properties.bedrock_type: Carboniferous Sandstone (Gullane Formation / Craigleith Sandstone Member)
properties.stratigraphy: Glacial till over interbedded sedimentary sandstone, siltstone, and mudstone
properties.lithic_notes: Dense, fine-grained, pale-ochre Craigleith and Hailes quarry quartz-arenite ashlar with high resistance to atmospheric weathering

properties.surface_paving: Whinstone (basaltic) sett carriageway with cut Craigleith sandstone flagstone walkways
properties.curb_specifications: Dressed granite and sandstone boundary curbs, drop kerbs, recessed basement lightwells with wrought-iron spearhead balustrades
properties.wear_patina: Historical micro-weathering, slate soot runoff patterns on horizontal string courses

properties.vegetation: Mature broadleaf trees in central private crescent gardens (Ulmus glabra, Tilia x europaea, Acer pseudoplatanus)
properties.canopy_density: Dense seasonal canopy adjacent to curvilinear carriageway

properties.typology: Georgian Neoclassical Terraced Crescent (Lord Moray Estate / James Gillespie Graham, 1822-1824)

structures.name: Ainslie Place Crescent Quadrant
structures.facade_material: Finely dressed buff Craigleith sandstone ashlar with channelled rustication at ground floor
structures.roof_geometry: Pitched Scottish slate roofs with lead flashings, hidden gutters, and stone chimney stacks
structures.fenestration: Symmetric 12-pane and 6-pane timber sash-and-case windows set in deeply recessed, square-moulded surrounds with continuous horizontal cornices and band courses
structures.plumb_rectification: Rigid vertical ashlar piers, plumb facade planes following the circular plan arc, level string courses

properties.street_furniture: Traditional cast-iron streetlamps and intact cast-iron area railings
